validation.rangeOrder: The end of the range must not be below its start
validation.interfaceToken: Interface tokens must be non-empty, without spaces or commas
validation.ipv6Brackets: IPv6 literals must be bracketed, e.g. [2001:db8::1]
validation.hostToken: Hostname must be non-empty, without spaces or commas
validation.credentialsForbidden: This proxy protocol does not accept credentials
validation.credentialsRequired: This proxy protocol requires username and password
validation.encryptionMethods: Enable at least one encryption method
validation.preferRc4: Prefer RC4 requires both methods enabled
validation.userAgentReadOnly: This user agent value is read-only

session.reopenHint: Closes and reopens all listen and outgoing sockets — use after the host's network configuration changed.

intro.speed: Rate limits are in bytes per second; setting a limit to 0 removes it. Peers on your local network are never rate limited.
intro.queueing:
Torrents set to "Auto managed" are queued: the client starts and pauses them on its own so that only a limited number is active at a time. The limits below say how many may be active in each category; −1 means unlimited. Torrents that are not auto managed don't count against these limits.
Once a seeding torrent meets any of the seeding goals at the bottom, it is considered done and yields its slot, but may keep seeding whenever a slot is free.
intro.trackers: A torrent can list several trackers, grouped into numbered tiers. Normally the client works through tier 0 in order and only moves to the next tier when a whole tier fails; the first two options change that. Timeouts and intervals are in seconds.
intro.advanced: Expert settings, exposed directly from the underlying BitTorrent engine. The defaults are sensible; careless changes can hurt performance or connectivity.

fields.listenSystemPortFallback: Fall back to a random port
fields.announceToAllTrackers: Announce to all trackers in a tier
fields.noRecheckIncompleteResume: Skip recheck on bad resume data

help.uploadRateLimit: Caps how fast all torrents combined may upload.
help.downloadRateLimit: Caps how fast all torrents combined may download.
help.dhtUploadRateLimit: Caps the average bandwidth the DHT itself may use. While over the cap, incoming DHT requests are dropped instead of answered.
help.rateLimitIpOverhead: Counts an estimate of TCP/IP packet overhead against the rate limits, so total network usage stays under them — not just the torrent data itself.
help.mixedModeAlgorithm: How bandwidth is divided when some peers are connected over TCP and others over uTP. "Prefer TCP" lets TCP peers use the whole limit; "Peer proportional" splits it according to how many peers use each protocol.
help.connectionsLimit: The most peer connections the client may have open at once, across all torrents. Every torrent is always allowed at least two connections, so with very many torrents the effective number can exceed a low limit.
help.connectionsSlack: How many incoming connections may be accepted above the connection limit, so newcomers can be compared against current peers and possibly replace them.
help.peerTransports: Which transports may carry peer connections, per direction. TCP is the classic transport; uTP runs over UDP and automatically yields to other traffic on your connection. Disabling both for a direction blocks that direction entirely.
help.outgoingInterfaces: Network adapters (by name) or local IP addresses that outgoing connections must use. Leave the list empty to let the operating system choose the route.
help.outgoingPortRange: Forces outgoing peer connections to use source ports from this range. Almost everyone should leave this disabled and let the operating system pick free ports.
help.anonymousMode: Hides identifying details where possible: trackers see a generic client name, your address is not attached to tracker requests, and peers are not told the client version. This is not an anonymity network — your IP address remains visible to everyone you connect to.
help.maxFailcount: How many times connecting to a peer may fail before the client stops trying that peer. A successful connection resets the count.
help.minReconnectTime: Base delay, in seconds, before retrying a peer after a failed connection. Each additional failure multiplies the wait.
help.peerConnectTimeout: How many seconds an outgoing connection attempt may take before counting as failed. Stalled attempts occupy connection slots and delay other peers.
help.connectionSpeed: How many outgoing connection attempts are started per second. 0 stops making outgoing connections altogether.
help.enableIpNotifier: Notices when the machine's network changes (new IP address, switched networks) and reconnects automatically. Disable this only if it misbehaves on your system — then use "Reopen network sockets" on the Session & about page after a change.
help.listenInterfaces: Where to accept incoming peer connections. Use 0.0.0.0 for every IPv4 interface, a device name (e.g. eth0) to bind one adapter, or a bracketed IPv6 address. Port 0 asks the operating system for a random free port. "Local" endpoints are not announced to trackers or the DHT beyond your own network.
help.listenSystemPortFallback: If the configured listen port is already taken, listen on a random port chosen by the operating system instead of failing.
help.maxRetryPortBind: If the listen port is taken, also try this many consecutive ports above it before giving up.
help.enableUpnp: Asks your router to forward the listen and DHT ports to this machine via UPnP, so peers on the internet can reach you without manual router configuration.
help.enableNatpmp: Asks your router to forward the listen and DHT ports using NAT-PMP/PCP — an alternative to UPnP supported mainly by Apple and newer routers. Both services can be on at once.
help.natpmpGateway: Sends NAT-PMP requests to this router address instead of auto-detecting the default gateway. Leave empty for automatic detection. Takes effect the next time NAT-PMP is started.
help.upnpIgnoreNonrouters: Ignores UPnP replies from devices outside your own subnet, so the client cannot accidentally configure somebody else's router.
help.upnpLeaseDuration: How many seconds a UPnP port mapping lasts before it is renewed. Set 0 for a permanent mapping if your router mishandles expiring ones; otherwise keep this at 5 minutes (300) or more.
help.natpmpLeaseDuration: How many seconds a NAT-PMP/PCP port mapping lasts before it is renewed.
help.announceIp: IP address reported to trackers in place of the one they observe. Normal trackers ignore or reject this; leave it empty unless you also operate the tracker (e.g. a seed running on the tracker host).
help.announcePort: Port reported to trackers and the DHT instead of the actual listen port. Useful only when peers must reach you through a different external port, such as a reverse tunnel; 0 reports the real listen port.
help.enableDht: Runs a node in the distributed hash table, which finds peers without any tracker and is what magnet links usually rely on to fetch their metadata.
help.enableLsd: Looks for peers on your local network by broadcasting which (non-private) torrents you have — handy when several machines on one LAN share a swarm.
help.useDhtAsFallback: Only asks the DHT for peers on torrents whose trackers have all failed, instead of using it alongside trackers all the time.
help.dhtBootstrapNodes: Well-known hosts contacted once at startup to join the DHT network. The defaults are fine for nearly everyone; with an empty list the DHT can only learn nodes from peers it happens to meet.
help.dhtAnnounceInterval: How many seconds pass between announcing each torrent to the DHT.
help.encryption: Encrypted connections can hide BitTorrent traffic from simple traffic shaping. Per direction: "Forced" allows only encrypted connections, "Enabled" allows both, "Disabled" allows only plain ones. The plaintext method obfuscates just the handshake, while RC4 scrambles the entire stream.
help.chokingAlgorithm: How upload slots are assigned while downloading. "Fixed slots" serves a fixed number of peers (the upload-slots setting); "Rate based" keeps opening slots as long as doing so still improves your upload rate.
help.seedChokingAlgorithm: Which peers get served while seeding. "Round robin" rotates fairly through peers; "Fastest upload" favors peers we can push data to quickest; "Anti leech" favors peers that are just starting or almost finished.
help.unchokeSlotsLimit: The most peers allowed to download from you at the same time, across all torrents. −1 removes the limit so every interested peer is served. Ignored when the choking algorithm is rate based.
help.optimisticUnchokeInterval: Seconds between rotating the optimistic unchoke — a trial upload slot given to a random peer in the hope of discovering better trading partners.
help.numOptimisticUnchokeSlots: How many trial upload slots to keep open. More slots find good peers faster but spend more bandwidth on strangers. 0 automatically uses a fifth of your upload slots.
help.suggestMode: Whether to hint to peers which pieces to request from us. "Read cache" suggests pieces already held in memory, which are cheap to serve.
help.maxPexPeers: The most peer addresses accepted from a single peer through peer exchange (PEX). Peers claiming to know more than this are capped at this number.
help.userAgent: The client identity announced to trackers and peers. Presenting a well-known client can matter on trackers with client allow-lists — but misrepresenting the client may break their rules.
help.handshakeClientVersion: Client name and version text sent to peers when a connection is established. Leave empty to derive it from the client identity above.
help.peerFingerprint: Short code at the start of the generated peer ID that tells the swarm what client software this is.
help.alwaysSendUserAgent: Repeats the user-agent header on every request to a web seed, instead of only the first request per connection. Some strict HTTP servers require this.
help.activeDownloads: How many auto managed torrents may be downloading at once.
help.activeSeeds: How many auto managed torrents may be seeding at once.
help.activeChecking: How many torrents may be checking their files at the same time.
help.activeLimit: Hard ceiling on active auto managed torrents overall — downloads and seeds combined, including slow ones.
help.activeDhtLimit: How many torrents may announce themselves to the DHT.
help.activeTrackerLimit: How many torrents may announce to their trackers.
help.activeLsdLimit: How many torrents may announce on the local network.
help.dontCountSlowTorrents: Torrents that are not actually transferring anything stop counting against the download and seed slots, making it likelier that your bandwidth is fully used. The two thresholds below define "slow".
help.inactiveDownRate: A torrent can be considered slow once it downloads below this rate, in bytes per second — it must also stay under the upload threshold for the whole startup grace period.
help.inactiveUpRate: The matching upload-rate threshold for considering a torrent slow, in bytes per second.
help.autoManageInterval: How often the queue is re-evaluated and rotated, in seconds.
help.autoManageStartup: For this many seconds after starting, a torrent always counts as active, giving it a fair chance to find peers before it can be judged slow.
help.autoManagePreferSeeds: When there aren't enough slots for everything, hand them to seeding torrents rather than downloading ones.
help.incomingStartsQueuedTorrents: If a peer finds and contacts us about a torrent that queueing has paused, start the torrent and serve the peer instead of turning it away.
help.seedTimeLimit: A torrent that has seeded for this many seconds has met its seeding goal.
help.seedTimeRatioLimit: Seeding goal as time: reached when time spent seeding hits this percentage of the time spent downloading.
help.shareRatioLimit: Seeding goal as data: reached when uploaded data hits this percentage of downloaded data (200 = uploaded twice as much as downloaded).
help.announceToAllTiers: Announces to one tracker from every tier instead of stopping at the first tier that works. This matches µTorrent's behavior rather than the multi-tracker standard.
help.announceToAllTrackers: Announces to every tracker within a tier in parallel, instead of only the first one that responds.
help.preferUdpTrackers: When the same host offers both UDP and HTTP trackers, try the UDP one first regardless of tier order. UDP announces are lighter for both sides.
help.maxConcurrentHttpAnnounces: The most HTTP tracker announces allowed in flight at once; further announces wait in a queue.
help.trackerCompletionTimeout: The most seconds an entire tracker request may take, from sending it to receiving the full response.
help.trackerReceiveTimeout: Seconds without receiving any data from a tracker before the request is abandoned — the timeout that fires when a tracker is down.
help.stopTrackerTimeout: Seconds to wait for the final "stopped" notice sent when a torrent is removed or the client shuts down; kept short so quitting stays quick. 0 skips these notices entirely.
help.trackerBackoff: How steeply retry delays grow for a failing tracker, in percent. 100 is the normal backoff; higher backs off faster, lower retries more aggressively.
help.minAnnounceInterval: Never announce to a tracker more often than this many seconds, even if the tracker asks for it — protects misconfigured trackers from being hammered.
help.autoScrapeInterval: Paused auto managed torrents are scraped — asked for their seed and downloader counts — this often, in seconds. Queueing uses the counts to decide which torrents deserve a slot.
help.autoScrapeMinInterval: At least this many seconds between any two automatic scrapes overall, keeping scrape traffic bounded when many torrents sit paused.
help.validateHttpsTrackers: Checks the certificates of HTTPS trackers and web seeds against the system's certificate store. Disable only if your system lacks a certificate store and secure trackers stop working.
help.applyIpFilterToTrackers: The session's IP filter also blocks tracker connections, not just peer connections.
help.proxy: Routes traffic through a SOCKS or HTTP proxy. Whether peer and tracker connections are proxied is chosen separately below, and DNS lookups can go through the proxy too, keeping torrent activity away from your local resolver.
help.i2p: Joins the I2P anonymity network through the SAM bridge of an I2P router running on your machine or network. Traffic travels through layered tunnels — more hops are more anonymous but slower.
help.diskIoCache: Whether the operating system may cache torrent data in memory, chosen separately for reads and writes. "Write through" still uses the cache but pushes data to disk immediately; disabling the cache lowers memory use at some speed cost.
help.mmapWriteMode: How downloaded pieces reach the disk when files are memory-mapped: via plain writes, via the memory mapping, or chosen automatically per situation.
help.mmapFileSizeCutoff: Files smaller than this are accessed with plain reads and writes instead of memory mapping. Measured in 16 KiB blocks.
help.hashingThreads: Threads used to verify piece hashes during a full recheck; these threads also do the reading. Keep at 1 for hard drives — more only helps on SSDs. Normal downloading verifies on the regular disk threads.
help.aioThreads: Number of threads performing disk reads and writes.
help.checkingMemUsage: How much data to keep in flight while checking torrents, in 16 KiB blocks. A larger budget makes rechecks faster but uses more memory.
help.maxQueuedDiskBytes: The most downloaded data, in bytes, allowed to wait in memory for the disk. When the queue is full, downloading pauses until the disk catches up — setting this very low throttles download speed.
help.filePoolSize: The most files kept open at once. Files are closed lazily because closing can be costly (some antivirus software scans on every close), but operating systems also limit open files per process.
help.closeFileInterval: Every this many seconds, the file that has been open the longest is closed, nudging the operating system to flush its disk cache — needed on Windows to keep the cache from growing without bound. 0 turns the periodic closing off.
help.noAtimeStorage: Opens files without updating their last-accessed timestamps, which can slightly improve disk performance. Linux only.
help.diskDisableCopyOnWrite: Marks downloaded files as "no copy-on-write" on Linux. This avoids heavy fragmentation on btrfs, but such files lose checksumming and compression and are harder to reflink. Alternatively, set the flag on your download folder yourself and leave this off.
help.optimisticDiskRetry: After a disk-write error puts a torrent into upload-only mode, retry writing after this many seconds to see whether the problem (like a full disk) has been fixed. Applies to auto managed torrents.
help.allowedFastSetSize: How many pieces peers may request even while choked, granted through the fast extension so new peers can get started immediately.
help.allowIdna: Allows trackers and web seeds with internationalized (non-ASCII) hostnames. Off by default because look-alike Unicode names can be abused for spoofing attacks.
help.allowMultipleConnectionsPerIp: Accepts more than one connection from the same IP address. Normally such connections are rejected to prevent abuse; allowing them makes duplicate-peer detection less reliable and is not recommended.
help.allowMultipleConnectionsPerPid: Accepts several connections claiming the same peer ID. Can improve transfers with peers that have multiple addresses, at the cost of extra network load.
help.autoSequential: Downloads torrents that have plenty of seeds in order instead of rarest-first. That is easier on the disk, and with that many seeds the download order hardly matters to the swarm.
help.banWebSeeds: Stops using a web seed for the rest of the session once it serves data that fails verification.
help.closeRedundantConnections: Drops connections that no longer benefit either side — for example when both ends already have the complete download.
help.connectSeedEveryNDownload: Downloading torrents get priority for new peer connections; every this-many attempts, one connection goes to a seeding or finished torrent instead.
help.dhtAggressiveLookups: Keeps the maximum number of DHT queries in flight at all times, querying closer nodes as soon as they are discovered. Lookups finish faster at the cost of more outstanding traffic.
help.dhtBlockRatelimit: A DHT node sending more packets per second than this (averaged over 10 seconds, so bursts are fine) is temporarily banned.
help.dhtBlockTimeout: How many seconds a DHT node stays banned after exceeding the packet-rate threshold above.
help.dhtEnforceNodeId: Ignores DHT nodes whose ID wasn't correctly derived from their address (BEP 42), answering their queries with an error. Makes identity-spoofing attacks harder.
help.dhtExtendedRoutingTable: Enlarges the first DHT routing-table buckets to 128, 64, 32 and 16 entries (instead of 8 everywhere), letting this node know a larger part of the network.
help.dhtIgnoreDarkInternet: Discards DHT messages arriving from address ranges where no legitimate traffic should originate.
help.dhtItemLifetime: Seconds before data items stored in this DHT node expire. 0 keeps them forever.
help.dhtMaxDhtItems: The most data items this DHT node will store on behalf of the network.
help.dhtMaxFailCount: Failed contact attempts before a node is dropped from the DHT routing table. Only matters when no replacement is waiting — failing nodes with a stand-by replacement are swapped out immediately.
help.dhtMaxInfohashesSampleCount: The most info-hashes included in a sample reply to other DHT nodes (BEP 51). Very large values may be clamped so replies still fit into UDP packets.
help.dhtMaxPeers: The most peer addresses this node stores per torrent on behalf of the DHT.
help.dhtMaxPeersReply: The most peer addresses returned in a single reply to a DHT get-peers request.
help.dhtMaxTorrents: The most torrents this node tracks for the DHT — an upper bound so malicious nodes cannot make it use unbounded memory.
help.dhtPreferVerifiedNodeIds: Gives preference in the routing table to nodes whose IDs are correctly derived from their addresses (BEP 42).
help.dhtPrivacyLookups: Performs DHT lookups in a slightly more expensive way that leaks less information about what you are looking for.
help.dhtReadOnly: Uses the DHT without serving it: other nodes won't keep us in their routing tables and incoming queries go unanswered. Meant for battery- or traffic-sensitive devices.
help.dhtRestrictRoutingIps: Refuses DHT routing-table entries with suspiciously similar IP addresses (same /24 network, or /64 for IPv6) and allows each IP only one entry, mitigating spoofing attacks.
help.dhtRestrictSearchIps: Applies the same similar-address restriction to nodes encountered during DHT searches.
help.dhtSampleInfohashesInterval: Seconds between recomputing the info-hash sample served to other DHT nodes (BEP 51). Allowed range 0–21600.
help.dhtSearchBranching: How many DHT queries run in parallel during a lookup (the 'alpha' parameter from the Kademlia paper).
help.handshakeTimeout: Seconds to wait for a peer's handshake reply before dropping the connection.
help.inactivityTimeout: A connection where neither side has had anything the other wants for this many seconds is closed.
help.initialPickerThreshold: A torrent's first pieces (this many) are picked at random so downloading starts quickly; after that, the rarest pieces are fetched first.
help.listenQueueSize: How many incoming connections the operating system may hold queued while we're busy. 5 suits normal use; raise it only for server-like deployments with heavy incoming traffic. Applied when the listen interfaces are next updated.
help.localServiceAnnounceInterval: Seconds between announcing each torrent to the local network.
help.maxAllowedInRequestQueue: How many block requests a single peer may queue up with us. A longer queue lets one peer download from us faster.
help.maxHttpRecvBufferSize: The largest HTTP response accepted when announcing to trackers or fetching .torrent files from a URL, in bytes.
help.maxMetadataSize: The largest torrent metadata (fetched for magnet links) accepted, in bytes.
help.maxOutRequestQueue: The most block requests kept outstanding to a single peer no matter how fast it is. Takes precedence over the request queue time.
help.maxPausedPeerlistSize: The known-peers list size used for paused torrents. Kept smaller than the regular list to save memory, since paused torrents don't need many candidates.
help.maxPeerlistSize: The most known peers remembered per torrent (candidates, not connections — so much larger than the connection limit). Eviction starts at 90% full; at the limit no new peers are added. 0 removes the limit.
help.maxPeerRecvBufferSize: The most memory one peer connection's receive buffer may grow to, in bytes.
help.maxPieceCount: The most pieces allowed in metadata received via magnet links. Extremely large torrents may need a higher limit to load.
help.maxSuggestPieces: The most piece suggestions remembered per peer, so a peer flooding suggest messages cannot waste memory.
help.maxWebSeedConnections: The most simultaneous web seed connections per torrent.
help.metadataTokenLimit: Parsing limit for torrent metadata received from peers, protecting against maliciously complex data. Very large torrents may need it raised.
help.noConnectPrivilegedPorts: Refuses outgoing connections to peers on ports below 1024, so the client cannot be tricked into hammering real services (a denial-of-service precaution).
help.noRecheckIncompleteResume: When resume data is missing or incomplete, assume nothing was downloaded and start fresh instead of checking what is already on disk.
help.numWant: How many peers to ask for in each tracker announce.
help.peerDscp: Priority tag (DSCP field) stamped on packets sent to peers, which routers may use to deprioritize bulk traffic. 0 means no marking; 1 is Lower Effort (RFC 8622).
help.peerTimeout: Seconds without any activity before a peer connection is closed. The protocol specifies 120; a keep-alive is sent at half this time.
help.peerTurnover: The percentage of peers disconnected in each turnover round to make room for trying new ones.
help.peerTurnoverCutoff: Turnover only runs while a torrent is close to its connection limit — above this percentage of it.
help.pieceExtentAffinity: Prefers downloading 4 MiB runs of adjacent pieces, which improves disk throughput on torrents with small pieces.
help.pieceTimeout: Seconds from sending a piece request until it counts as timed out when no data comes back.
help.predictivePieceAnnounce: Announces pieces to peers this many milliseconds before they finish downloading and verifying, saving round trips. 0 disables the prediction.
help.prioritizePartialPieces: Prefers completing already-started pieces over starting rare ones. When off, rare pieces win unless partial pieces pile up out of proportion.
help.rateChokerInitialThreshold: Starting threshold of the rate-based choking algorithm. A higher value opens fewer upload slots; a lower one opens more.
help.recvSocketBufferSize: Receive buffer size for peer sockets, in bytes; 0 keeps the operating-system default. Note that uTP peers, the DHT and UDP trackers share one UDP socket buffer per listen interface — if it is too small, packets get dropped.
help.reportRedundantBytes: Includes discarded duplicate data in the upload totals reported to trackers.
help.reportTrueDownloaded: Reports the true downloaded amount to trackers, counting redundant data, instead of only the useful payload.
help.reportWebSeedDownloads: Counts data fetched from web seeds in tracker reports and in the client's own statistics and download rates.
help.requestQueueTime: Target depth of the request pipeline to each peer, expressed as seconds of transfer it should hold — faster peers automatically get deeper queues.
help.requestTimeout: Seconds to wait for a requested 16 KiB block before requesting it from a different peer instead.
help.resolverCacheTimeout: Seconds before cached DNS lookups expire. Failed lookups are remembered for an eighth of this time.
help.seedingOutgoingConnections: Lets seeding and finished torrents initiate connections themselves. Turning this off saves connection budget in setups where downloaders can always reach you directly.
help.seedingPieceQuota: While seeding, serve a peer this many pieces before rotating its upload slot to another peer.
help.sendBufferLowWatermark: Minimum data kept ready to send per peer (including data still being read from disk), in bytes. Should fit at least a few 16 KiB blocks for snappy seeding — it acts as the initial window that determines how fast uploads ramp up.
help.sendBufferWatermark: Upper bound on data buffered for sending to one peer, in bytes. Too small hurts upload capacity; too large wastes memory.
help.sendBufferWatermarkFactor: Scales each peer's send buffer with the current upload rate to it, in percent (50 = half a second's worth), capped by the watermark above. Values above 100 can improve upload throughput on fast connections.
help.sendNotSentLowWatermark: Limits how much unsent data the kernel buffers per socket (Linux's TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT option), in bytes. 0 leaves the system default.
help.sendRedundantHave: Tells peers about completed pieces even when they already have them. Not normally useful, except for some statistics collection.
help.sendSocketBufferSize: Send buffer size for peer sockets, in bytes; 0 keeps the operating-system default.
help.shareModeTarget: Target upload ratio for torrents in share mode: at 3, the client tries to upload three times what it downloads. Below 2 is pointless; very high values are so conservative that nothing may ever be downloaded.
help.smoothConnects: Spreads connection attempts evenly over time when close to the connection limit, instead of connecting in bursts that then also time out in bursts.
help.ssrfMitigation: Restricts tracker and web seed requests that point back into your machine or local network — a request-forgery precaution. Loopback trackers must use conventional announce paths, and web seeds on private addresses are limited.
help.strictEndGameMode: Near the end of a download, only requests a block from a second peer once every remaining piece has a request outstanding. Avoids downloading duplicate data, at the cost of some end-game speed.
help.supportShareMode: Advertises support for the share-mode extension to peers; disabling prevents its use.
help.tickInterval: Milliseconds between the internal ticks that hand out bandwidth quota. Lower values (around 100) give finer rate limiting; higher values save CPU. Keep at 1000 or below — negative values are for testing only.
help.torrentConnectBoost: How many peers to connect immediately when a torrent's first tracker response arrives, instead of waiting for the once-per-second scheduler. At most 255.
help.udpTrackerTokenExpiry: Seconds to reuse UDP tracker connection tokens; the specification says 60. Higher values save packets, but only work if the tracker keeps tokens valid equally long.
help.unchokeInterval: Seconds between re-evaluating which peers get upload slots. The protocol suggests 30 — long enough for TCP to reach full speed before the next shuffle.
help.urlseedMaxRequestBytes: The largest byte range requested from a web seed in one HTTP request. Bigger requests are cheaper per byte, but one request covering a whole file prevents fetching it in parallel.
help.urlseedTimeout: Like the peer timeout but for web seeds, in seconds — usually shorter, since web servers are expected to be reliable.
help.urlseedWaitRetry: Seconds before retrying a failed web seed, when the server doesn't say via a Retry-After header.
help.useParoleMode: Peers that took part in a piece that failed verification may only download whole pieces until they prove themselves; if a solo piece from such a peer fails too, the peer is banned.
help.utpConnectTimeout: Milliseconds before the first uTP connection packet times out; each consecutive timeout doubles the wait.
help.utpCwndReduceTimer: After packet loss shrinks uTP's transfer window, don't shrink it again for this many milliseconds, even if more packets are lost.
help.utpFinResends: How many times the closing packet is resent before a uTP socket is torn down forcibly.
help.utpGainFactor: The most bytes the uTP transfer window may grow per round trip. Too high overreacts to measurement noise; too low reacts sluggishly to congestion.
help.utpLossMultiplier: How much the uTP transfer window shrinks on packet loss, as a percentage of its size. Never set this above 100.
help.utpMinTimeout: The shortest allowed uTP packet timeout, in milliseconds. The real timeout follows the connection's latency but never drops below this floor.
help.utpNumResends: How many times a lost packet is resent before the uTP connection is given up.
help.utpSynResends: How many connection-attempt packets are sent before giving up on establishing a uTP connection.
help.utpTargetDelay: The queueing delay uTP aims to cause, in milliseconds. Higher values are more aggressive and queue more data at the bottleneck; too low, and measurement noise makes it send too slowly.
help.webSeedNameLookupRetry: Seconds to wait before retrying a failed DNS lookup for a web seed.
help.wholePiecesThreshold: Peers fast enough to deliver an entire piece within this many seconds are asked for whole pieces at a time — friendlier to disk caches, and bad peers are easier to identify when a piece fails.
